stories.headline: PM adviser fired after investigation exposes EU-funded ghost trainings; FNTT and STT open criminal inquiries
stories.summary: A 15min.lt investigative report with hidden camera footage revealed that a company owned by PM Ruginienė's public affairs adviser Vigilijus Jukna received EU funds for farmer training sessions that took place in empty rooms. Ruginienė dismissed Jukna the same day the story broke; the Financial Crimes Investigation Service (FNTT) and Anti-Corruption Commission (STT) subsequently opened pre-trial investigations and searched his premises. President Nausėda called on Ruginienė to address the matter; Jukna's lawyer denied wrongdoing.

stories.headline: Dawn of Nemunas coalition partner raided by financial crimes investigators; coalition stability questioned
stories.summary: Lithuanian financial crimes investigators (FNTT) conducted searches at the offices and parliament cabinet of Dawn of Nemunas (Nemuno Aušra) chairman Remigijus Žemaitaitis over suspected irregularities in a vehicle lease arrangement. LSDP leader Sinkevičius said the raids would not by themselves determine the party's future in the coalition, while Ruginienė stated trust in law enforcement; the LRT described parliament as resembling a crime drama season amid the wave of raids and suspicions. Nausėda had separately expressed doubts about ministries under Dawn of Nemunas' oversight.

stories.headline: US presses Lithuania to resume Belarus potash transit; Vilnius rejects pressure, demands Belarus concessions first
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Budrys confirmed publicly that the US had lobbied Lithuania to reopen Klaipėda port to Belarus potash exports, currently under EU sanctions. President Nausėda denied experiencing 'pressure' while acknowledging diplomatic exchanges; PM Ruginienė's adviser reiterated no negotiations were occurring; ex-PM Šimonytė urged calm; LSDP leader Sinkevičius said the subject was 'speculative' since EU sanctions run to February and discouraged public discussion.

stories.headline: Vilnius airport repeatedly shut by Belarus smuggler balloons; Lithuania to declare emergency situation
stories.summary: Vilnius airport halted operations overnight on May 13 for the second time in a week after detection of what Lithuanian authorities identified as smuggler balloons from Belarus drifting into its airspace; Lithuania formally protested to Belarus twice. PM Ruginienė announced the government would declare a state of emergency the following week. Lithuania accuses Belarusian President Lukashenko of enabling smuggling operations using weather balloons to transport cigarettes across the border.

stories.headline: Nausėda and Stubb call for stronger NATO eastern flank air defenses after wave of drone incidents
stories.summary: Lithuanian President Nausėda and Finnish President Stubb met in Vilnius on May 14 and jointly stated that recent drone incursions across Baltic and Nordic airspace underscore the urgency of improving detection and interception capabilities. Nausėda warned 'warring parties' not to use Lithuanian territory for drone overflights, acknowledged gaps in existing defenses, and called Lithuania a growing European defense industry hub. The meeting followed a series of drone incidents affecting the Baltic states.

stories.headline: Lithuania and Ukraine sign full Drone Deal at Bucharest summit, covering joint production and technology transfer
stories.summary: On the sidelines of a Bucharest summit, Lithuanian President Nausėda and Ukrainian President Zelensky signed a bilateral agreement under the 'Drone Deal' framework covering joint production of long-range strike, naval, interceptor and bomber drones, technology transfer between companies, and deployment of Ukrainian defense experts to Lithuania. The summit also included other Baltic and Nordic leaders discussing Ukraine peace steps.

stories.headline: Ignitis Group posts Q1 revenue growth and releases 2026–2029 strategy focused on green flexibility and grid expansion
stories.summary: State-owned energy company Ignitis Group reported Q1 2026 revenues of €939 million (up 34% year-on-year) and EBITDA of €175.4 million, though net profit fell 13% to €72.8 million. The group simultaneously published its 2026–2029 strategic plan targeting 2.8–3.2 GW of installed green capacity and an adjusted EPS of €3.5–4.0 by 2029, with strategic focus on green flexibility, electricity networks, and data centers. A battery storage shipment arrived at Kruonis pumped-storage plant.

stories.headline: Lithuania and Latvia offer to host US troops as Pentagon suspends European rotation; Nausėda urges caution on troop picture
stories.summary: Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas confirmed the US had paused its troop rotation to Europe pending a Pentagon deployment review; foreign ministers of Lithuania and Latvia publicly offered to host more US soldiers should troops withdraw from Germany. President Nausėda on May 17 cautioned against premature conclusions, saying the final disposition of US forces in Europe was likely not yet determined; he also said Lithuanian troops could potentially serve in a Hormuz strait mission if US-Iran peace were achieved.

stories.headline: State Auditor finds major 2025 budget reporting errors; Ruginienė demands accountability over misused public funds
stories.summary: Lithuania's State Audit Office published findings identifying significant misstatements in 2025 state budget execution reports, including €916.8 million in expenditures not disclosed by their actual purpose. PM Ruginienė responded by demanding accountability from the Social Security Ministry and Sodra over double-payment of childcare benefits, and also named the Lithuanian Riflemen's Union as requiring greater financial transparency.

stories.headline: Baltic $14 billion defense build-up; Lithuania positions itself as regional defense industry hub
stories.summary: At a Lithuanian Defence and Security Industry Association conference on May 12–13, President Nausėda stated Lithuania was becoming one of Europe's most important defense industry centers, citing Rheinmetall ammunition production and KNDS equipment assembly. Defense News reported the Baltic states collectively planning $14 billion in defense spending. Foreign Minister Budrys criticized European countries not spending enough, and NATO's supreme commander praised Lithuania as a model. Carnegie Endowment published analysis on how Baltic states are hedging against a possible US withdrawal from NATO.

stories.headline: Suspected Ukrainian military drone crashes in Lithuania
stories.summary: Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre confirmed on May 17 that a suspected Ukrainian military drone was found crashed on Lithuanian territory. The government provided no further details in the snippet beyond confirming the finding.

articles.title: Suspected Ukrainian military drone was found crashed in Lithuania, authorities say

stories.headline: Latvia drone crisis and PM resignation provide backdrop to Lithuania's own airspace security debates
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a fuel depot in Latvia, triggering the resignation of Latvian Defence Minister Sprūds and subsequently Latvian PM Siliņa; multiple drones from Russia and Ukraine crossed Baltic airspace within 48 hours. Lithuanian officials and media closely tracked these events as context for Lithuania's own drone/airspace vulnerability, and Lithuanian Defence Minister Kaunas cited Russian drones falling in three Baltic states within 48 hours when calling on NATO to strengthen regional defenses.
